column1: What is the fundamental architectural invariant underpinning SageMaker's design regarding data and compute?
column2: Separation of stateful model artifacts (persisted in S3) from stateless, ephemeral compute resources (transient EC2 instances), ensuring data durability and reproducibility without persistent cluster management.

column1: In SageMaker's container contract, where must training data be mounted and where must model artifacts be written?
column2: Training data is mounted at /opt/ml/input; model artifacts must be written to /opt/ml/model.

column1: How does SageMaker Feature Store resolve the tension between training-time and inference-time feature access requirements?
column2: Via a dual-path (bifurcated) storage architecture: an offline store (S3 + Glue) for immutable, timestamped historical data enabling point-in-time correctness, and an online store (low-latency key-value store) for single-digit millisecond real-time inference serving.

column1: Why does the offline Feature Store use microsecond-precision monotonically increasing event timestamps?
column2: To enable precise time-travel queries during training dataset construction, preventing label leakage by ensuring only historically valid feature values are used.

column1: What are the three physical invariants that must be internalized before architecting distributed training systems?
column2: 1) Compute is cheap relative to memory bandwidth (communication often bottlenecks over arithmetic); 2) Gradient synchronization is a collective operation where the slowest worker sets the effective clock rate; 3) Parallelism strategies (data, tensor, pipeline) compose but do not commute—optimal configuration is empirical, not fixed.

column1: What environment variables does SageMaker inject into training containers to describe distributed cluster topology?
column2: SM_HOSTS, SM_CURRENT_HOST, and SM_NUM_GPUS, among others—establishing rank, local rank, and world size for each node.

column1: What is the core function of AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) in distributed training?
column2: EFA is a network interface that bypasses the OS kernel for inter-node messaging via RDMA, serving as the high-performance substrate for collective communication operations (e.g., gradient all-reduce) across training nodes.

column1: How do SageMaker's deployment mechanisms reflect practical CAP theorem trade-offs?
column2: Real-time endpoints prioritize availability/partition tolerance over strict consistency (eventual consistency in scaling/metrics); batch transform favors throughput/cost over latency; asynchronous inference uses a queue to decouple request submission from processing.

column1: How does SageMaker ensure atomic rollback and reproducibility of deployed models?
column2: Through a content-addressed storage model where each model version is identified by an immutable S3 URI; rollback is achieved by repointing endpoint configurations to a previous URI without data corruption or partial state propagation.

column1: What are the three core invariants distinguishing production SageMaker Pipelines from experimental ML workflows?
column2: 1) Parametric determinism (identical inputs yield bit-identical outputs); 2) Lineage immutability (artifacts cryptographically bound to provenance metadata, append-only audit trail); 3) Monotonic versioning (pipeline DAG itself versioned as code, tied to exact commit hash).

column1: In SageMaker Model Monitor, what is the distinction between data quality drift and model quality drift?
column2: Data quality (covariate) drift: P(X) changes while P(Y|X) remains stable. Model quality (concept) drift: P(Y|X) itself evolves, meaning the underlying function being approximated changes.

column1: What is the core architectural invariant underlying all four SageMaker Model Monitor dimensions (data quality, model quality, bias drift, feature attribution drift)?
column2: Constraint-based anomaly detection: production behavior expectations are encoded as statistical bounds derived from a baseline, and alerts trigger when live observations violate those bounds beyond a defined threshold.
